gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: The hotel is comfortable; ___, it is far too expensive.
She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we arrived ___ the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly... when' is the fixed pair for one event interrupting another.

gaps.sentence: ___ a staffing shortage, the clinic closed early.
gaps.explanation: 'Due to + noun phrase' states the cause in formal register.

gaps.sentence: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a full clause; due/owing take noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: I noted down the reference number ___ I needed it later.
gaps.hint: just in case it proved necessary
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = because it might be needed later; no purpose is intended.
